references.text: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said. This shows the same pattern of Pharaoh's hardened heart.
When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his own heart and did not listen to them. The same reaction from Pharaoh after a plague.
Pharaoh hardened his heart again this time and would not let the people go. A repeated motif of Pharaoh's hardened heart.
Pharaoh sinned once more and hardened his heart. This shows Pharaoh's persistent hardness and lack of repentance.
Whoever is often rebuked but hardens their neck will suddenly be broken beyond healing. The theme of hardening one's heart against warnings.
Take it to heart - the contrast with Pharaoh, who did not take it to heart (לֹא־שָׁת לִבּוֹ).
He poured out his burning wrath on them, but they did not take it to heart. The same expression about not taking God's actions to heart.
Both illustrate the active choice Pharaoh makes to harden his own heart as a direct consequence of turning away from God's commands.
Both verses demonstrate that Pharaoh uses every pause or relief to actively harden his heart even further.
Highlights the theological tension between God's sovereign hardening and Pharaoh's own active resistance.
Complements 7:23 by showing how Pharaoh's own resistance fits into God's sovereign plan to harden his heart.
9:35 confirms and summarizes the stubbornness established early in 7:23 when Pharaoh turned away from the warning.
Complements 7:23 by balancing Pharaoh's own resistance with God's sovereign action to harden his heart.
